Find snapped locations of input points on street network

Source: R/network_tools.R
find_snap.Rd

Finds where points snap to the street network: snapping is how routing places origins and destinations on the network. The nearest point of a street the mode may use is looked for first within 300 metres of the point and then, if there is none, within radius. A point that does not snap is not routed. The street a point snaps to depends on the mode, since some streets cannot be used by some modes (a pedestrian street cannot be used to snap car trips).

Usage

find_snap(network, points, radius = 1600, mode = "WALK")

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network().

points

Either a POINT sf object with an id column, in any coordinate reference system (reprojected to WGS 84, see travel_time_matrix()), or a data.frame containing the columns id, lon and lat (WGS 84).

radius

Numeric. The maximum radius in meters within which to snap. Defaults to 1600m.

mode

A string. Which mode to consider when trying to snap the points to the network. Defaults to WALK, also allows BICYCLE and CAR.

Value

A table with the original points (point_id, lat, lon), their snapped coordinates on the street network (snap_lat, snap_lon), the distance in meters between the point and its snapped location (distance, haversine on a sphere of radius 6,367,450 m) and whether the point snapped (found). Points that could not be snapped have NA coordinates and distance and found = FALSE.

Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package). A data.table result has an index on found (when options(datatable.auto.index) is on, as by default).

See also

Other network functions: build_network(), check_transit_availability(), get_gtfs_errors(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf(), transit_network_to_sf()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))
snaps <- find_snap(network, points, radius = 2000, mode = "WALK")
head(snaps)
